impact: Adds export risk to Nvidia's results tonight and weighed on Asian chip stocks Tuesday; indirect pressure on the AI hardware chain including MU, DRAM and SNXX.
summary: The Commerce Department issued an interim rule Monday requiring data-center customers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil to get a special license to buy advanced AI chips from US firms such as Nvidia and AMD. It also bans offshore data centers from providing significant computing to companies in arms-embargoed countries like China, and formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. It follows scrutiny of Singapore-based Megaspeed over possible chip diversion and comes days before Trump's China trip.
title: US rule requires licenses for AI chip sales to 5 countries, curbs China remote access
